text:
You grade one workflow job of Rho-Bank's procedure library against an answer key. An answering
agent serves customers by following this job exactly, as it is shown below (its steps, conditions,
arguments, rules and the facts it asks for; the quotes behind them are not shown to the agent).
For each fact in the key, decide whether the job leads the agent to it; for each trap, decide
whether the job tells the agent to do it. Judge only what the job says, not what a good agent
would know without it.

Facts:
- right: a step, an argument or a rule leads the agent to the fact for every case the fact names.
- partly: it does for some of the cases the fact names and is silent on the others, or it says
  it so loosely that an agent following it could give another answer.
- missing: nothing in the job leads the agent to it; the agent would have to work it out alone.
- wrong: the job leads the agent to a different answer for at least one case the fact names, even
  if it is right for others.

Traps:
- present: a step, an argument or a rule tells the agent to do it, for some case.
- absent: nothing in the job does.

Then list the conflicts: two steps, arguments or rules that give the same case different
instructions, so an agent could follow either.

Job: pin_lock_investigation_protocol

  "note": "customer: only when the customer reports a debit card declined or locked because of the PIN (CODE 55, 75 or 83). The agent then runs the investigation for every locked card before any unlock. The agent offers closure, replacement, disputes, a PIN reset or a security-team transfer only on the paths the protocol names. It does any of them only when the customer accepts. The one exception is 3+ prior locks, where the protocol makes a PIN reset required instead of an unlock."

 "info": [

  },

 "steps": [
  {
   "id": "identify",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "Look up the customer by name, email or id. Ask for 2 of: date of birth, email, phone, address. Compare the answers with the records.",
   "call": "get_user_information_by_name",
   "args": {
    "customer_name": "the customer's stated name (or get_user_information_by_email / _by_id with what they gave)"
   },
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "check_identity",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "Confirm that at least 2 values match the record from identify. Share no card or account information before they match. If they still do not match after asking again, tell the customer you cannot verify them and stop.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "identify"
   ],
   "after": [
    "identify"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "time",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Get the current time for the verification log and for the date math.",
   "call": "get_current_time",
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [
    "identify"
   ],
   "if": "two values match"
  },
  {
   "id": "log_verif",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Log the verification.",
   "call": "log_verification",
   "args": {
    "name": "verified user's name",
    "user_id": "verified user id",
    "address": "record address",
    "email": "record email",
    "phone_number": "record phone",
    "date_of_birth": "record DOB",
    "time_verified": "time from get_current_time"
   },
   "lookup": [
    "check_identity"
   ],
   "after": [
    "time"
   ],
   "if": "two values match"
  },
  {
   "id": "accounts",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Unlock and call the tool that lists all of the user's bank accounts, with tier, status, balance and date_opened.",
   "call": "get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847",
   "args": {
    "user_id": "the verified user"
   },
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [
    "log_verif"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "cards",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Unlock the tool, then call it once for each checking account to get its debit cards with their pin_locked and pin_lock_reason fields.",
   "call": "get_debit_cards_by_account_id_7823",
   "args": {
    "account_id": "each checking account id"
   },
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [
    "accounts"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "txns",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Unlock the tool, then call it once for each account with a locked card to get the declined attempts and recent successful activity.",
   "call": "get_bank_account_transactions_9173",
   "args": {
    "account_id": "each checking account with a locked card"
   },
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "if": "a card has pin_locked = TRUE"
  },
  {
   "id": "ask_which_card",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If several cards are affected, ask which one the customer wants to discuss first and go through the cards in that order. Still finish investigating every locked card (check_other_locked) before unlocking any of them.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "after": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "if": "more than one of the customer's cards is declined or locked"
  },
  {
   "id": "ask_circumstances",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "For each locked card, ask the customer what happened: where they were, roughly when, and what amount they tried. Ask before you mention the location, time or amounts in the records, and never reveal the scoring. Compare their account with the declined transactions in txns when you score the card and ask the follow-up questions.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [
    "txns"
   ],
   "if": "a card has pin_locked TRUE and the customer has not yet described how it was locked"
  },
  {
   "id": "not_locked_branch",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the card's pin_locked is FALSE but pin_attempts_remaining is low, tell the customer how many attempts remain before the card locks. If they forgot the PIN, offer a PIN reset (unlock_and_post_unlock_pin_reset).",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "after": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "if": "the card's pin_locked is FALSE and pin_attempts_remaining is low"
  },
  {
   "id": "code_83_branch",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the decline was a PIN verification or network error (CODE 83) and the card is not locked, explain that the PIN was not wrong and advise retrying. If it keeps failing, suggest a signature transaction, a different terminal or merchant, or waiting 10-15 minutes.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "after": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "if": "the decline was 'unable to verify PIN' (CODE 83) and pin_locked is FALSE"
  },
  {
   "id": "triggers",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "For each locked card, check the automatic triggers first:\n- A security_hold card cannot be unlocked here; it goes to the security-hold transfer offer.\n- If several cards are locked, investigate every card before unlocking any of them.\n- If a card was replaced as stolen in the last 90 days, enhanced verification is required.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards",
    "txns",
    "time"
   ],
   "after": [
    "txns"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "check_security_hold",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "For each locked card, read pin_lock_reason. If it is 'security_hold', do not score or unlock the card. Offer to transfer the customer to the security team for that card, and keep handling the customer's other cards normally.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "after": [
    "triggers"
   ],
   "if": "a card has pin_locked TRUE"
  },
  {
   "id": "security_hold_transfer",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the customer accepts the offer, transfer with reason fraud_or_security_concern. The summary names the card on security hold and what was done for the other cards. Transfer after the other cards are handled, unless the customer asks to go now.",
   "call": "transfer_to_human_agents",
   "args": {
    "summary": "card with pin_lock_reason security_hold needs security team review; outcomes for the customer's other cards",
    "reason": "fraud_or_security_concern"
   },
   "lookup": [
    "check_security_hold"
   ],
   "after": [
    "check_security_hold"
   ],
   "if": "pin_lock_reason = 'security_hold' AND the customer accepts the transfer offer"
  },
  {
   "id": "security_hold_declined",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the customer declines the transfer, acknowledge it and tell them they can contact Rho-Bank later about that card. Do not unlock, reset or otherwise act on it. Close the conversation politely once the other cards are done.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "check_security_hold"
   ],
   "after": [
    "check_security_hold"
   ],
   "if": "pin_lock_reason = 'security_hold' AND the customer declines the transfer"
  },
  {
   "id": "security_hold_last",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "When the customer has a security-hold card and other locked cards, finish every other card first: its unlock, PIN reset, closure and replacement. Make the security-hold transfer last, because the transfer ends the chat. If the customer asks to go now, tell them which cards are still open before you transfer.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "check_security_hold",
    "cards"
   ],
   "after": [
    "check_security_hold"
   ],
   "if": "a card has pin_lock_reason 'security_hold' and the customer has other locked cards still to handle"
  },
  {
   "id": "check_other_locked",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If more than one card has pin_locked TRUE, finish investigating and scoring every locked card before unlocking any of them. Each card gets its own score and outcome.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards"
   ],
   "after": [
    "triggers"
   ],
   "if": "more than one card has pin_locked TRUE"
  },
  {
   "id": "check_recent_stolen",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If any card on the account has issue_reason 'stolen' with date_issued within 90 days of get_current_time, standard verification is not enough for an unlock. No enhanced-verification tool is documented, so do not unlock; follow cannot_unlock_options.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards",
    "time"
   ],
   "after": [
    "triggers"
   ],
   "if": "a card on the account has issue_reason 'stolen' and date_issued within 90 days"
  },
  {
   "id": "score",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "Score each card that has no security hold, using flags A1-A3 (location), B1-B3 (time), C1-C4 (amount), D1-D3 (card history) and E1-E3 (account). Never reveal the calculation to the customer.\n- A1: declined city vs the address city: same 0, other city same state 1, other state 2, other country 3. A2: 2 locations 1, 3+ locations 2. A3: all successful 7-day transactions at home but declines elsewhere +1.\n- B1: hour of the attempt: 6AM-10PM 0, 10PM-12AM 1, 12-2AM 2, 2-6AM 3. B2: last successful PIN use 7-30 days ago 1, over 30 days 2. B3: gap between attempts 2-5 min 1, 1-2 min 2, under 1 min 3.\n- C1: decreasing amounts 2. C2: all round hundreds 1. C3: 2-5x the average ATM withdrawal 1, over 5x 2. C4: 80-100% of daily_atm_limit 1, attempts totalling over the limit 2.\n- D1: 1, 2 or 3+ prior locks in 90 days score 1, 2 or 3. D2: card age 1-3 months 1, under 1 month 2. D3: another card with a velocity block +1, with a fraud alert +2.\n- E1: account age 3-6 months 1, under 3 months 2. E2: 1 overdraft 1, 2+ overdrafts 2. E3: balance $50-100 1, under $50 2.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards",
    "txns",
    "accounts",
    "identify",
    "time"
   ],
   "after": [
    "triggers",
    "check_security_hold",
    "check_other_locked",
    "check_recent_stolen"
   ],
   "if": "pin_lock_reason is not 'security_hold'"
  },
  {
   "id": "ask_location",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the score is 5 or higher and a location flag scored, ask whether the customer was at the location of the declined attempt. If yes, remove the location flags and rescore. If no, keep the score and proceed with caution.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "score"
   ],
   "if": "score >= 5 and location flag scored"
  },
  {
   "id": "foreign_location_denied",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "Sometimes the declines were in a different country (A1 = 3) and the customer says they were not there. Keep the location flags in that case. If the customer also answers the time question with 'I was asleep' or similar, the card is CRITICAL: do not unlock it. Go to check_unauthorized, then recommend closure and replacement (cannot_unlock_options). The customer still having the physical card does not change this.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "ask_location",
    "ask_time",
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "ask_location"
   ],
   "if": "A1 is a different country and the customer denies being at that location"
  },
  {
   "id": "ask_time",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the time-of-day flag scored 2 or more, ask whether the customer was using the card at that time. If they confirm, remove the time flag. If they say they were asleep or similar, treat the card as CRITICAL (likely fraud).",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "score"
   ],
   "if": "time-of-day flag >= 2"
  },
  {
   "id": "ask_amount",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the amount-pattern flag scored, read back the attempted amounts and ask whether the customer remembers them. If they confirm, remove the flag. If they deny it or seem confused, keep it.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "score"
   ],
   "if": "amount pattern flag scored"
  },
  {
   "id": "velocity_flag_stays",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "B3 scores 3 when consecutive failed attempts are less than 1 minute apart. The Step 4 questions remove only location, amount-pattern and time-of-day flags, never B3. So even when the customer confirms the attempts were theirs (for example, mistyping in a rush), the card keeps a 3-point flag. Do not unlock it; follow single_flag_escalation, check_unauthorized and cannot_unlock_options. Explain that the speed of the attempts triggered a security protocol, without revealing the scoring.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "txns"
   ],
   "after": [
    "score"
   ],
   "if": "the card's consecutive failed attempts were less than 1 minute apart (B3 = 3)"
  },
  {
   "id": "medium_question",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "For a final score of 5-7, ask: 'I see failed PIN attempts on your card. Were those attempts yours?' Unlock only if the customer says yes (for example, they were at that store and may have mixed up PINs). If they say no, follow cannot_unlock_options.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "ask_location",
    "ask_amount"
   ],
   "after": [
    "ask_location",
    "ask_time",
    "ask_amount"
   ],
   "if": "the card's recalculated score is 5-7"
  },
  {
   "id": "decide",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "Apply the thresholds to each card:\n- 0-4: unlock.\n- 5-7: unlock only after asking whether the attempts were the customer's.\n- 8-10: unlock only if the customer confirms and gives a satisfactory explanation.\n- 11-14: no unlock on this call.\n- 15+, or a customer who denies an overnight attempt: CRITICAL. Go to the fraud closure path (check_unauthorized, then the closing job).\n- 3+ prior locks: PIN reset instead of unlock.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "ask_location",
    "ask_time",
    "ask_amount",
    "medium_question"
   ],
   "after": [
    "ask_location",
    "ask_time",
    "ask_amount",
    "medium_question"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "three_plus_locks_reset",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the card has had 3 or more prior PIN locks in the last 90 days, do not unlock it, and do not route it to cannot_unlock_options for this reason alone. Tell the customer that, because the card has been locked several times recently, it cannot simply be unlocked and needs a new PIN. Run unlock_and_post_unlock_pin_reset (three_plus_reset) for that card. Never reveal the scoring.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "cards",
    "score",
    "decide"
   ],
   "after": [
    "decide"
   ],
   "if": "D1 for the card is 3 or more prior locks in 90 days, and the card has no other cannot-unlock condition (no other 3-point flag, not CRITICAL or 11-14 without the D1 points, attempts not denied, no trigger)"
  },
  {
   "id": "single_flag_escalation",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If any single flag on the card other than D1 still scores 3 points after the questions (for example, a 2-6 AM attempt the customer did not make), do not unlock. The card needs supervisor review: follow check_unauthorized and cannot_unlock_options, which include the security-team transfer. D1 at 3+ prior locks goes to three_plus_locks_reset instead.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "score",
    "ask_time",
    "ask_location"
   ],
   "after": [
    "decide"
   ],
   "if": "any single flag other than D1 lock frequency equals 3 points"
  },
  {
   "id": "very_high_branch",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "For a final score of 11-14, tell the customer the card cannot be unlocked on this call. No callback or enhanced-verification tool is documented, so offer the cannot_unlock_options.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "decide"
   ],
   "after": [
    "decide"
   ],
   "if": "the card's final score is 11-14"
  },
  {

## The answer key

- K1 (overnight_denial): declined attempts in another US state between 2 AM and 6 AM that the customer denies, saying she was asleep at home, make the card CRITICAL (likely fraud): it is not unlocked, whatever the total; the job reaches this for a different state, not only for a different country
- K2 (critical_outcome): a CRITICAL card with no successful unauthorized transaction is recommended for closure and replacement because fraud is suspected, and on the customer's yes it is closed and a replacement ordered for the same checking account (the closing and the order may run in the jobs this one names)
- K3 (suspicious_period): the suspicious period checked for successful unauthorized transactions is the window of the declined attempts the customer denies (from the first of them to now): successful transactions before it, her usual home-city activity, are not put to her as possibly unauthorized and not disputed, so a card whose period holds only declined attempts gets no dispute and she is told no money was taken
- K4 (admitted_attempts): a card whose declined attempts the customer confirms were hers (at that store, at that time, for that amount: she mixed up PINs) has its location flags removed and its score recalculated, and with no 3-point flag, fewer than 3 prior locks and a recalculated score of 10 or less it is cleared for unlock: not closed, not escalated, not sent to the cannot-unlock options
- K5 (card_order): locked cards on different checking accounts are taken one at a time, in the order the customer chooses, each to its outcome before the next is investigated; the trigger to finish investigating every locked card before any unlock applies only to locked cards on the same checking account
- K6 (two_prior_locks): a card cleared for unlock with 2 prior PIN locks in the last 90 days must be asked 'This is your third PIN lock in 90 days. Would you like me to reset your PIN to a new number?', and on a yes its PIN is reset to the new PIN the customer chooses (reset_debit_card_pin_6284, here or in the PIN-reset job this one names)
- K7 (security_hold): a card with pin_lock_reason security_hold is not scored, unlocked or reset: the agent offers a transfer to the security team, and when the customer declines it does nothing more on that card (no transfer, no write)

## The traps

- T1: every locked card the customer has, on any checking account, is investigated and scored before any of them is unlocked (the same-account trigger applied across accounts)
- T2: a PIN reset is offered, beside closure and a transfer, for a CRITICAL card (one whose overnight attempts the customer slept through); the reset clears the lock, so taking it unlocks a card that cannot be unlocked
- T4: the suspicious period reaches back before the first declined attempt the customer denies (to the last transaction she confirms as hers, or over the recent successful activity), so earlier home-city transactions she does not recognise are put to her and disputed
